articles.title: Chicago Bears: Motivated Pass Rusher Avoids IR (For Now), Out Week 6
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears’ EDGE rusher room cannot catch a break lately. The NFL suspended one-time Pro Bowler Montez Sweat for the next two games without pay for vi...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears' EDGE rusher room cannot catch a break lately. The NFL suspended one-time Pro Bowler Montez Sweat for the next two games without pay for violating the league's Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy, prompting many fans to argue that the alleged substances he was taking weren't working, given his measly production of 13 pressures and two sacks over five games. Sweat will forfeit approximately $2.3 million, and his remaining guarantees have been voided. Meanwhile, Dayo Odeyingbo suffered a quadriceps injury during the third quarter of last week's game and did not return.

The Chicago Bears' motivated pass rusher avoids IR, out Week 6

During Wednesday's press conference, Ben Johnson told the media that Dayo Odeyingbo will likely miss some time as he recovers from a quadriceps injury, as reported by Chris Kwiecinski of FOX 32 . The good news is that Odeyingbo likely won't go on injured reserve, per Patrick Finley of The Chicago Sun-Times. With Odeyingbo expected to miss time, the defense must rely on a handful of inexperienced pass rushers.

This leaves the Bears with only four healthy EDGE rushers on the active roster: Austin Booker , Shemar Turner , Daniel Hardy, and Jamree Kromah. Turner was activated from the PUP list on Tuesday after missing the first five games to recover from a right ACL tear. Chicago may sign an EDGE rusher to the practice squad since they do not have any on the practice squad.

articles.title: Five wickets in an over: South African bowler makes history with rare feat - Watch
articles.summary: Chad Laycock made history on Tuesday by becoming the first bowler to take five wickets in an over in South African T20 cricket.
articles.body: Chad Laycock made history on Tuesday by becoming the first bowler to take five wickets in an over in South African T20 cricket. The 19-year-old achieved the feat while playing for KZN Inland against Titans in the CSA Pro20 Cup in Pietermaritzburg.Laycock finished with career-best figures of 6/26, including a record of four wickets in four consecutive deliveries in South African T20 cricket. Among Full Member teams in T20 internationals, Lasith Malinga, Rashid Khan, Curtis Campher and Jason Holder have previously achieved the four-wicket sequence.Laycock also set a new record for the best bowling figures in CSA Pro20 Cup history, going past Beuran Hendricks' 6/29 from 2014.The historic over came in the 19th over of the Titans innings. Laycock first dismissed Leus du Plooy before taking the wickets of Dayyaan Galiem, Aphiwe Mnyanda, Janco Smit and Esosa Aihevba off the next four deliveries. The five wickets ended Titans' innings at 204, with the team having been 193/4 before the over.Laycock had earlier given KZN Inland their first breakthrough by dismissing Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who scored 81 off 36 balls, in the ninth over. Pretorius and his opening partner had put together 112 runs.However, Laycock's performance was not enough to secure a win for KZN Inland. Chasing 205, they finished on 183/6, losing the match by 21 runs. Laycock remained unbeaten on 31. The victory extended table-toppers Titans' unbeaten run in the competition to six matches.Laycock became the fourth bowler known to have taken five wickets in an over in men's T20 cricket, as per Cricinfo. Bangladesh's Al-Amin Hossain, India's Abhimanyu Mithun and Indonesia's Gede Priandana had achieved the feat before him.Priandana remains the only bowler, male or female, to take five wickets in an over in a T20 international. He achieved the feat against Cambodia in December 2025.Al-Amin took five wickets in an over while playing for UCB-BCB XI against Abahani Limited in the 2013-14 Victory Day T20 Cup. Mithun achieved the feat in the 2019-20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy semifinal, playing for Karnataka against Haryana in India's domestic T20 competition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'India have totally spoiled Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's confidence': Former cricketer makes bold claim
articles.summary: India’s T20I team has several talented opening batters, including Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan and young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
articles.body: India’s T20I team has several talented opening batters, including Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan and young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.However, frequent changes in the playing XI have raised concerns about the team management’s approach, with former India captain Krishnamachari Srikkanth believing that the uncertainty has affected the confidence of both Samson and Sooryavanshi.Samson struggled in his first three matches against Ireland and England, scoring 5, 0 and 1.Sooryavanshi then made his T20I debut and scored 14, 13 and 15 in his first three games. Samson returned for the fifth T20I against England, scoring 27, but was rested for the Zimbabwe tour. Sooryavanshi took his opportunities on that tour, scoring 50, 20 and 81.Srikkanth questions team managementSrikkanth believes the team management should give young players more chances instead of constantly changing the opening combination. He suggested resting Abhishek Sharma and allowing Samson and Sooryavanshi to open together."They have not only spoiled his (Sanju Samson's) confidence, India have totally spoiled Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's confidence. He could have been given three matches against a team like the West Indies. Now that they've seen Abhishek for so long, he can be rested, and Sooryavanshi and Samson can open in the next match," Srikkanth said in a YouTube video.He also questioned Samson’s consistency. Although the wicketkeeper-batter played three important innings during India’s 2026 T20 World Cup triumph, including the final, his performances have since become less reliable."Samson has always been up and down. His consistency has always been questionable. He'll suddenly do wonders like the World Cup and then suddenly fail a lot. Someone like Abhishek Sharma never has such extremes. Now, again, Samson will score in the next match," Srikkanth said.West Indies level series after Hope’s centuryMeanwhile, India suffered a 24-run defeat against West Indies in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, leaving the five-match series tied at 2-2. West Indies posted 247/3, powered by Shai Hope’s unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and Sherfane Rutherford’s 49 not out.India started their 248-run chase strongly, with Samson smashing 56 off 20 balls. Abhishek added 29, while Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy put together 70 runs in 32 balls.However, Keemo Paul’s three wickets in the 19th over triggered a collapse, and India were bowled out for 223, falling short by 24 runs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sahibzada Farhan, now Pakistan's captain, surpasses India's Abhishek Sharma to script new T20I record
articles.summary: Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan created a new record by scoring 238 runs in a three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka, surpassing India's Abhishek
articles.body: Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan created a new record by scoring 238 runs in a three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka, surpassing India's Abhishek Sharma, who scored 229 runs against Afghanistan earlier this year.Farhan scored his third consecutive half-century, making 76 off 47 balls in the final match on Tuesday.Farhan breaks Abhishek Sharma’s recordFarhan now leads the list for the most runs in a bilateral three-match men's T20I series between two Full Member teams. New Zealand's Colin Munro is third with 223 runs, followed by Australia's David Warner with 217 and Afghanistan's Hazratullah Zazai with 204.Despite Farhan's strong performance, Pakistan lost the third T20I by eight wickets. The hosts scored 168/8, but Sri Lanka chased down the target with 17 balls remaining, thanks to Kusal Mendis's unbeaten 87 off 47 balls. Mendis was named Player of the Match.Pakistan had already won the series after victories in the first two matches, winning the opening game by four wickets and the second by 82 runs.After the final match, Farhan said Pakistan had followed the same plan as in the earlier games and stressed the importance of staying in form."The way we set a superb target in the first two matches, today also we had the same plan, but it's cricket; anything can happen. The effort is to stay consistent. When I perform well, I'm even more focused to do well in the next match. It's cricket; you're not always in form. So I'm looking to make the most of it," he said, as per the ICC website.Kusal Mendis praises Sri Lanka’s performanceSri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis praised his team's bowling, fielding and batting after the convincing win. He also highlighted Kamindu Mendis's contribution following the Powerplay."We bowled really well today in the middle period. The fielding was better too, and the batting was excellent. Kamindu (Mendis) batted really well after the Powerplay. He played his natural game, and I did too. We did really well in all three departments," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sanju Samson joins Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli in elite T20I club after quick 56 off 23 against West Indies
articles.summary: Sanju Samson added another milestone to his T20I career on Wednesday, becoming only the sixth Indian batter to hit 100 sixes in the format during the
articles.body: Sanju Samson added another milestone to his T20I career on Wednesday, becoming only the sixth Indian batter to hit 100 sixes in the format during the fourth T20I against West Indies at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium. The wicketkeeper-batter reached the landmark in style while launching India's pursuit of a daunting 248-run target, producing an explosive 56 off just 23 deliveries.Samson's aggressive innings featured six fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 243.48, giving India early momentum after West Indies captain Shai Hope struck an unbeaten century to power the visitors to 247/3. However, Samson's counterattack ended when Keemo Paul dismissed him for 56, with Shimron Hetmyer completing a catch near the boundary.Samson joins India's elite six-hitting clubWith 102 sixes to his name in T20Is, Samson has joined an exclusive group of Indian batters to have crossed the 100-six mark. Rohit Sharma leads the list with 205 sixes, followed by Suryakumar Yadav with 179.Abhishek Sharma, who had 141 sixes at the time of filing, is third on the list, while Hardik Pandya and Virat Kohli have struck 126 and 124 sixes, respectively.A productive year for SamsonThe milestone comes amid a productive year for the Kerala-born batter. Samson has scored 687 runs in 24 matches and innings in 2026, averaging 29.86 at a strike rate of 178.44. His tally includes seven half-centuries, with a highest score of 97 not out.One of the defining phases of his year came during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, when Samson registered three consecutive half-centuries, beginning with a Super Eight clash against West Indies and continuing through the final against New Zealand. His performances earned him the Player of the Tournament award and helped India secure their third T20 World Cup title.Samson's overall T20I recordIn 76 T20Is and 68 innings, Samson has accumulated 1,719 runs at an average of 27.28 and a strike rate of 158.87. articles.title: 'Got to look at luggage weight': Shai Hope jokes after winning third Player of the Match award during this India tour
articles.summary: West Indies captain Shai Hope reflected on his outstanding form after leading his team to a 24-run victory over India in the fourth T20I.
articles.body: West Indies captain Shai Hope reflected on his outstanding form after leading his team to a 24-run victory over India in the fourth T20I. His unbeaten century helped West Indies level the five-match series 2-2, setting up a decisive final match in Bengaluru on October 17. Hope has enjoyed a remarkable tour of India, collecting three Player of the Match awards so far.Hope joked about the difficulty of carrying his growing collection of awards back home, while stressing that his main goal is to help the team win."To be honest, those (POTM trophies) were a bit heavy; we got to look at luggage weight. So I think we are gonna have some problems when I go back home with those Player of the Match awards. I am just trying to give the team the best chance," he said."So as long as we lay that foundation at the start, we got a 50-plus opening partnership. So it was good for us to start innings and then obviously we got that foundation. You can express yourself a bit more in the middle period and then try to give the team the best finish as possible."Hope explains West Indies' strong totalWest Indies posted 247/3, with Hope scoring an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls, including four fours and nine sixes. Shimron Hetmyer contributed 33 off 12 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 deliveries.Hope said the pitch was more challenging than expected, making the total of over 240 runs a competitive score to defend."I honestly felt it was a decent score because the surface; it was actually holding a bit more than we thought initially. We felt as though the pitch would probably come on a bit better. But I found that with the new ball, some balls were kicking up a lot more and then some were staying down as well. So it is a bit too pace to start, and then obviously with the spinners and the quicks in the back end, it was a little bit more difficult to hit through the line. So I felt as though 240 plus was a decent score," he added.Hope enjoys a record-breaking run in IndiaHope has scored 601 runs in 16 T20I innings this year at an average of 50.08, including two centuries and four half-centuries. Across international cricket in 2025, he has accumulated 1,336 runs in 30 innings, with five centuries and seven fifties.His performances in India have been equally impressive. He has scored 278 runs in three ODI innings and 261 runs in four T20I innings. Across both formats, he has amassed 539 runs in seven innings, including four centuries and a half-century.India struggled in the chase despite Sanju Samson's 56 off 22 balls and a 70-run partnership between Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy. West Indies bowler Keemo Paul took five wickets for 41 runs, helping restrict India to 223.With the series tied at 2-2, both teams will compete for the trophy in the final T20I at Bengaluru's M. Chinnaswamy Stadium on October 17.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Captain Shai Hope continued his dream run, scoring his second century of the T20I series - an unbeaten 102 (50b; 4x4, 9x6) - while pacer Keemo
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Captain Shai Hope continued his dream run, scoring his second century of the T20I series - an unbeaten 102 (50b; 4x4, 9x6) - while pacer Keemo Paul bagged 5/41 as the West Indies defeated India by 24 runs to make it 2-2 and keep the fivematch series alive here at the Rajiv Gandhi International stadium on Wednesday.After the West Indies were put in to bat, Hope hit his third century in T20Is to power the visitors to 247/3. Later, Paul’s exploits on a batter-friendly wicket saw India finish at 223 in 19.3 overs as last batter Arshdeep retired hurt.Chasing a stiff target, Samson (56; 23b, 6x4, 4x6) launched into Shamar Joseph with consecutive sixes and Roston Chase with two boundaries and as many sixes to take India to 50 in three overs. He reached his half-century off just 20 balls while Abhishek Sharma played just three deliveries at the other end in that period. However, Samson departed after pulling Paul straight into the hands of Hetmyer at deep square leg.Ishan Kishan (6) also holed out to deep midwicket as the hosts went to 80/2 in the Powerplay. Captain Shreyas Iyer sliced Shamar Springer to backward point, reducing India to 97/3 in 8.2 overs. At the halfway stage, they were 115/3, needing 133 more for victory.However, Gudakesh Motie derailed the chase by striking twin blows in the 12th over. He first ended Abhishek’s uncharacteristic 29 (24b; 3x4, 1x6) as the batter holed out to longoff, followed by Naman Dhir being stumped first ball.Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy tried to keep their side in the hunt. Nitish took a special liking to Shamar Joseph, hitting him for 21 runs with a boundary and consecutive sixes in the 16th over to bring down the equation to 53 from five overs. However, Tilak (43; 25b, 2x4, 3x6) was caught at mid-off off Shepherd that reduced India to 200/6.There on, the chase proved too steep for the hosts. Paul removed Nitish (41; 20b, 1x4, 4x6), Prince Yadav and Axar Patel in four deliveries of the 19th over.Earlier, Jewel Andrew and Hope provided a quick start, putting 50 runs on the board in just 3.3 overs. Axar provided the breakthrough, dismissing Andrew (21; 16b, 2x4, 1x6) by trapping him in front. But Hetmyer maintained the momentum to take his side to 79/1 in the Powerplay.Prince removed Hetmyer (33; 12b, 4x4, 2x6) and at the half-way stage, West Indies were 118/2. Hope lofted Mayank for a six to reach his half-century in 28 balls.Arshdeep got rid of Rovman Powell (24; 17b, 2x4, 1x6) in the 13th over, but Sherfane Rutherford (49*; 26b, 4x4, 3x6) and Hope added an unbroken 91 runs in 43 deliveries to provide the final flourish. articles.title: Pragyan Ojha may continue as interim chief selector
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: There’s ambiguity around the composition of the BCCI’s national selection committee following former chief Ajit Agarkar’s decision not to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: There’s ambiguity around the composition of the BCCI’s national selection committee following former chief Ajit Agarkar’s decision not to continue. The deadline for applications to fill the West Zone vacancy ended on Wednesday with former India wicketkeeper Parthiv Patel, who was widely tipped to be Agarkar’s replacement, choosing not to apply for the job.VVS to have bigger say?Parthiv’s decision to opt out has given rise to speculation that the head of the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE), VVS Laxman, may have a greater say in selection affairs, with Pragyan Ojha continuing as the interim chairman of the selection committee. With the ODI World Cup less than a year away, will the BCCI choose to continue with the two?“BCCI would have preferred continuity with Agarkar staying on till the World Cup, but things didn’t go as expected. If a new chairman of selection committee comes in, there’s a chance his vision could be different from the ones working now. So, the board will have to gauge the vision of the new selector,” a BCCI source said, adding, “With Laxman’s growing influence, the board may let things remain the way they are at present.”It will be interesting to see if the board takes more time to find a suitable candidate for the chief selector’s role. Or else, it is likely it will proceed with candidates to just fill up the spot for a representative from the west zone.Board willing to increase budget to rope in big namesAccording to sources, the BCCI prefers ‘big’ names with a considerable amount of international cricket behind them to take up important positions. TOI has learnt that the board has become flexible in its pay policy to rope in the big names.Since RP Singh and Pragyan Ojha joined the selection committee in Sept last year, BCCI’s expenses on selection committees exceeded the annual budget by Rs 3 crore to Rs 17.45 crore. Interestingly, the board has reserved a budget of Rs 19.35 cr for 2026-27, marking an increase of another Rs 2 cr. That implies BCCI has increased the budget for the selection committees by Rs 5 cr.TOI understands that the board had reached out to a couple of former cricketers who have played close to 100 Tests, but they declined the offer. It is learnt that recent appointments in the men’s selection committee have happened with candidates negotiating their salaries.Will SS Das continue after Dec?The BCCI has to also deliberate if it wants to continue with SS Das as a selector since he will complete four years in the job in Dec. Sources said that there’s a chance that the board will let Das continue till the World Cup.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Don't like going out anymore': Prithvi Shaw opens up on life and his goal of India comeback
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At 26, Prithvi Shaw is determined to rebuild his cricket career by focusing on his game, family and work ethic while staying away from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At 26, Prithvi Shaw is determined to rebuild his cricket career by focusing on his game, family and work ethic while staying away from unnecessary distractions.Once regarded as one of India's brightest batting prospects, Shaw has faced several setbacks in recent years but remains committed to earning another opportunity in the national team.“I am working harder than ever before. Obviously, I am not quite on social media right now. I am just working on myself. Just me, my cricket and my family. Those are the only three things I am focusing on right now. Anything else, I am just trying to ignore or keep aside,” Shaw told India Today.When asked about whether he has grown tired of the off-the-field attention, he replied, “No, no, it is not about that. It is about a lot of these papparazzi people and all. And I just do not like going out anymore."I have my personal space, and obviously, you guys know how I am and what I like personally. It is good for other people; someone likes it, someone does not. I do not like cameras around me when I am living my personal life somewhere.”Shaw rose to national attention as a teenager after scoring 546 runs in a Harris Shield school cricket match in Mumbai.In 2018, he captained India to the Under-19 World Cup title and made an impressive start to his Test career with a century on debut against the West Indies.However, his international journey lost momentum after early success. He has played five Tests, six ODIs and one T20I for India, with his last international appearance coming against Sri Lanka in July 2021.Questions about his fitness, discipline and consistency, along with injuries, added to the challenges he faced.Learning from setbacksShaw's difficult period became more evident in 2024 when Mumbai dropped him from their Ranji Trophy squad. He also went unsold at the IPL 2025 mega auction after Delhi Capitals released him.Former India coach Greg Chappell later encouraged him through a letter, reminding him that past disappointments should not determine his future.Shaw now says he is less concerned about outside criticism and more interested in how his family sees him. He has also reduced his public outings, preferring to spend time in his hotel room watching Netflix or playing video games such as FIFA, GTA and Tekken.“I feel that comments from outside do not really matter to me. What matters is what my family thinks about me and how I am as a person. I know myself and what are the right things to do to achieve a milestone," he added."I might be wrong somewhere, and that is not an issue. No one is correct in this life. A lot of people, including you, might not be correct. Everyone goes through it. It is all about destiny, and I never look at the past anymore.”Despite the setbacks, Shaw showed encouraging form in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season, scoring 537 runs in seven matches, including a blistering 222 off 156 balls against Chandigarh. Delhi Capitals also brought him back for the 2026 IPL season, although he did not get an opportunity to play.India comeback remains ultimate goalShaw believes consistency will be crucial to his chances of returning to the national team, especially with several openers competing for places. He also wants to set a positive example for younger cricketers by maintaining strong work habits and putting the team's needs first.“If you want to get to the top, there is a big line of openers waiting to go up, so you have to be consistent enough to be there. I have always seen that my team comes first before I do, and I think that is what makes my consistency level better,” he remarked.For Shaw, the ambition to represent India again remains the biggest motivation, despite more than five years away from international cricket.“If that goal were not there, I would not even be playing today. Obviously, the ultimate goal, the biggest goal, is to go back there and return to the Indian team. It is not about proving anything to anyone. It is me versus me. That is it,” Shaw further noted.For now, Shaw is choosing to concentrate on improving himself rather than dwelling on past disappointments. His approach is simple: work harder, spend time with loved ones and let his performances speak for themselves.“I want to be with my guys, focus on cricket, focus on my work ethic and give more time to cricket. Then I go to the hotel room and play some PS5. That is it,” he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Indian team for the five-match ODI series for India's upcoming tour of New Zealand will be picked “in the next two-three days,” BCCI secretary
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Indian team for the five-match ODI series for India's upcoming tour of New Zealand will be picked “in the next two-three days,” BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI on Wednesday.“We will select India’s ODI team in the next two or three days,” Saikia told this paper.It's understood that pacers Prasidh Krishna and Harshit Rana will undergo a Return to Play (RTP) tests on Oct 24 or 26 at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, after which the selectors are likely to announce the Indian team for the two-Test series, set to start in Wellington from Nov 19.On Thursday, both the Indian men’s and women’s teams will be felicitated by India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their gold medal-winning campaigns at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan.The Pragyan Ojha-led selection committee has already picked India’s T20I squad for the five-match T20I series in New Zealand, which will start from Oct 22. The five-match ODI series will start on Nov 4 in Auckland. It's understood that Ojha met Team India captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir, celebrating his 45th birthday, in Hyderabad on Wednesday, for the first time since the BCCI asked him to take over as the interim chairman of the national selection committee.Amongst the newcomers, one of the strong contenders for a berth is Mumbai’s seam-bowling all-rounder Suryansh Shedge, who has emerged as a strong contender to earn his maiden ODI call-up following a couple of impressive performances in the recently-concluded List A series against Australia A in Puducherry.The 23-year-old Shedge, who played three T20Is for India in England, recently returned to competitive cricket after recovering from a hamstring injury and, replacing injured senior India allrounder Hardik Pandya, impressed with both bat and ball, taking four 40 four wickets with his seam bowling, and then scoring 66 in a winning cause in the final One-dayer.Pandya's prolonged absence from competitive cricket due to a spate of injuries, and the drop in performance and Pandya's next-best alternative, seam bowling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, may work in favour of Shedge, who is set to join the Mumbai team for its second 2026-27 season Ranji Trophy match against Himachal, which will start from Oct 18 in Bilaspur.The fifth ODI in Tauranga will be played on November 15, while the first Test in Wellington begins on November 19, which means that like New Zealand, India too will pick a 'split squad' for the ODI series, as a few regular India players may prepare with he red ball in order to prepare for a crucial World Test Championship series.Candidates interviewed for Junior selection panelMeanwhile, on Tuesday, the BCCI's two-member Cricket Advisory Committee comprising former India batters Ashok Malhotra and Jatin Paranjape interviewed a few candidates for the post of junior selection committee, via zoom call.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal articles.title: BCCI steps in to save Arunachal's domestic season
articles.summary: MUMBAI: With Arunachal Pradesh forfeiting its Ranji Trophy opener against Nagaland and missing participation in two age-group tournaments, the BCCI has
articles.body: MUMBAI: With Arunachal Pradesh forfeiting its Ranji Trophy opener against Nagaland and missing participation in two age-group tournaments, the BCCI has moved swiftly to ensure the state’s cricketers do not suffer further more of the administrative logjam.The board has constituted a three-member selection committee to pick Arunachal Pradesh’s men’s and women’s teams across age groups, paving the way for the state to continue its participation in the domestic season. This is despite a legal battle within Arunachal Cricket Association (ACA).The move follows Arunachal’s forfeiture of its opening Ranji Trophy fixture in Ahmedabad after the association failed to field a team. The state also missed Vinoo Mankad Trophy and Under-19 Women’s T20 Trophy as rival ACA factions remain embroiled in litigation before Itanagar Bench of Guwahati High Court.Thanks to BCCI’s intervention, however, Arunachal Pradesh is now expected to take the field for its next Ranji Trophy match against Sikkim in Nadiad from Oct 18.BCCI apex council member M Khairul Jamal Majumdar has been appointed convener of the arrangement. The selection panel consists of former Assam cricketers Satya Gopal Chakraborty, Jayanta Chowdhury and Deep Bora, with Chakraborty serving as chairman.The committee has been tasked with conducting trials and selecting teams for Ranji Trophy, Col CK Nayudu Trophy, Senior Women’s T20 Trophy and Vijay Merchant Trophy.Explaining the board’s decision, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said protecting players’ interests had been the overriding priority.“We have made our apex council member Khairul Mamun Mazumdar the convener and appointed three selectors who have been conducting the entire process over the last three days. The BCCI wants to ensure that no player is denied opportunities because of circumstances beyond their control. We have a robust domestic structure and every player deserves a chance to showcase his or her talent,” Saikia told TOI on Wednesday.Drawing parallels with a similar situation in Bihar in the past, Saikia said the board had adopted the same approach by appointing an independent mechanism to keep cricketing activities on track.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ: Can New Zealand stop India's big hitters? Mitchell Santner reveals his plan
articles.summary: New Zealand white-ball captain Mitchell Santner is under no illusions about the challenge that awaits his side against India’s explosive top order.
articles.body: New Zealand white-ball captain Mitchell Santner is under no illusions about the challenge that awaits his side against India’s explosive top order. With the likes of Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Sanju Samson capable of dismantling bowling attacks from the outset, Santner knows the Black Caps will need more than discipline to keep the visitors in check.As New Zealand prepare for the five-match T20I series, the left-arm spinner is hoping the early-season conditions offer some assistance, while stressing the need for his bowlers to adapt quickly and stay in the contest even when the boundaries begin to flow.“ They pack power all the way through and come out with a lot of aggression. As a bowler, you know there aren’t going to be too many dot balls. You have to plan accordingly, assess the conditions and use them to your advantage,” Santner said.The New Zealand captain acknowledged that boundaries would inevitably come against such an aggressive opposition, but stressed that bowlers must focus on the deliveries between them.“Even if you get hit for boundaries, it is about what happens with the balls in between. Those could be wicket-taking deliveries or dot balls. If we can restrict India to around 200 in New Zealand, that might be a good score, considering the power they possess,” he added.The prospect of facing Abhishek, Ishan and Sanju has prompted Santner to emphasise tactical flexibility, particularly during the powerplay. The early-season pitches in Christchurch could offer movement.“If the ball moves, we need to use that to counter their explosive batting. But if the pitch is flat, then we might have to create pressure, by using the bigger boundaries and finding different ways of taking wickets,” he said.Santner acknowledged that the power-packed nature of modern T20 cricket has made life increasingly difficult for bowlers, with even conceding 30-40 runs in a spell potentially representing a good performance.“If you can take two or three wickets for around 30 or even under 40 runs, you are probably doing a very good job. Against someone like Abhishek or Ishan, you know they will come hard from ball one. You have to decide whether that means bowling yorkers, arm balls or taking the ball away from their hitting arc,” he explained.Santner also acknowledged the threat posed by young sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Having seen the teenager’s exploits in the IPL, the New Zealand captain expects India’s power-hitters to test his bowlers from the outset.“I’ve seen what he can do at the IPL. Whether it is Sooryavanshi, Abhishek, Ishan or Sanju, India have power throughout the lineup. It will be a challenge to stop him.”Santner also acknowledged that India could arrive with a point to prove following New Zealand’s historic 3-0 Test series triumph on Indian soil and a 2-1 ODI series victory.“You never like losing a series at home. The more you play in places like India, the better equipped you become to handle the conditions. India might have a point to prove, but our job is to play what is in front of us and beat a very good team at home,” he said.With Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma continuing to attract enormous attention for the ODIs, Santner expects the tour to bring its share of excitement.“Rohit and Kohli may not be getting any younger, but they are still churning out the runs.”(Watch India tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV starting October 22, 2026).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Mahipal Lomror holds firm to help Rajasthan earn 3 points against Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Mahipal Lomror scored a gritty 84 that helped Rajasthan secure three vital points against Tamil Nadu as the four-day Ranji Trophy Elite Group D
articles.body: JAIPUR: Mahipal Lomror scored a gritty 84 that helped Rajasthan secure three vital points against Tamil Nadu as the four-day Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match ended in a tame draw at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium here on Wednesday. TN had to be happy with one point after they had conceded the 89-run first-innings lead on Tuesday.Tamil Nadu needed a few quick wickets in the first session on Day 4 to give themselves a chance for victory but Mahipal and Kartik Sharma shattered their hopes with a solid 78-run stand for the fourth wicket. Extending their stay from 81/4 on Day 3, Mahipal and Kartik not only denied the visitors any wicket but also scored at a fairly quick pace to take the game beyond their reach.By the time, Kartik (42: 75b, 4x4, 2x6) got out trying to sweep Sai Kishore for another boundary, the hosts were more or less in a safe zone. Ajay Singh Kukna then frustrated the opponents by providing solid support to Mahipal.Mahipal’s second half-century of the match and his 83-run stand for the sixth wicket with Kukna (32*: 79b, 3x4) closed the door on TN’s comeback bid. After Mahipal was finally dismissed for 84 (170b, 7x4), Manav Suthar declared the innings giving an impossible-looking target of 282 in less than two sessions.The visitors did not make any effort to chase and settled for some batting practice reaching 73/0 at tea break. Sai Sudharsan, who got out for just 3 in the first innings, remained unbeaten on 26, while fellow opener Narayan Jagadeesan made 45 not out, when the match was called off.TN skipper Sai Kishore and newly-appointed coach Yo Mahesh did not seem too disappointed with the result.“There are several positives from this season-opener. Deepesh Devendran impressed with his three-wicket haul on debut. Experienced seamer Saravana Kumar also made a strong comeback, while Andre Siddharth batted brilliantly to keep our hopes alive on the third day. Sai Kishore gave us early breakthroughs in the second essay,” Yo Mahesh said.Sai Kishore felt the lower-order collapse put them on the backfoot. “We had a fairly good start with both Jagadeesan and Pradosh hitting fifties. Then Baba Indrajith and Andre kept us in the hunt but once that unfortunate run out of Sonu Yadav happened it did affect our march towards taking the first-innings lead. Rajasthan bowlers especially Kukna bowled really well,” said Sai Kishore.Yo Mahesh rued the fact that they couldn’t make use of their chances.“We had our chances but we couldn’t latch on to those. In the second innings we had Rajasthan reeling at 31/4 and we should have capitalised on it. Credit must be given to Mahipal and Kartik for the way they batted and frustrated us. The toss, too, played a critical role,” said Yo Mahesh.Manav was pleased with the result and lauded his young team for getting the better of their strong opponents."Certainly it was a very good result for us. Tamil Nadu is traditionally a formidable side with a couple of India players in their ranks. We did really well to start with three points. It's a positive beginning for us in the season," Manav told TOI after the match.Three players -- Rohan Rajbhar, Chetan Sharma and Hemant Kumar -- made their debut for Rajasthan, who also missed the services of regular bowlers like Khaleel Ahmed, Aniket Choudhary, Deepak Chahar and Rahul Chahar."We went into the match with an inexperienced side but debutants Rohan and Chetan did remarkably well. Even Karan Lamba returned to the side after two years and struck an important hundred. Kukna's five-wicket haul turned the match in our favour and Mahipal batted well in both the innings. Overall it was almost a perfect start for us," said Manav, who will leave for New Zealand in a couple of days to join India 'A' side.BRIEF SCORESRajasthan 363 and 192/6 declared in 34 overs (Mahipal Lomror 84, Kartik Sharma 42, Ajay Singh Kukna 32*; Sai Kishore 3-50 ). articles.summary: KALYANI: Bengal coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla exuded quiet confidence at the end of Day Three on Tuesday, when Delhi needed 88 runs more with seven wickets in
articles.body: KALYANI: Bengal coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla exuded quiet confidence at the end of Day Three on Tuesday, when Delhi needed 88 runs more with seven wickets in hand to make the hosts bat again, with the hope of preventing them from recording an outright win.The bowlers did live up to the challenge as Bengal made a winning start to their Ranji campaign, beating Delhi by nine wickets in their Elite Group ‘C’ clash at the Bengal Cricket Academy (BCA) ground here on Wednesday.While Bengal ended with six points, Delhi have plenty to ponder as they returned empty-handed. However, the hosts were guilty of missing out on bagging maximum points (7), as they lost opener Ankur Paul caught by Dev Lakra off Hrithik Shokeen while going for a big shot in the 89-run victory chase.On a day when seven wickets fell to spin, it was the lesser known Sumanta Gupta who made the difference.Delhi made a good start on the last day with Ayush Badoni and Anuj Rawat managing to see off the tricky first hour. Bengal tasted first blood when Rawat was clean bowled attempting a rather unnecessary reverse sweep off Aamir Gani to be clean bowled.But, Yash Dhull, who retired hurt last evening, came out to give his skipper good support as the duo started to rebuild the innings.Easwaran then threw the ball to Gupta for the last over before lunch and the part-time off-spinner provided the much-needed breakthrough with his second delivery of the match. Dhull stretched forward as the ball bounced up hitting the pad and then kissed his gloves to land into the safe hands of wicketkeeper Abishek Porel.The opener felt not allowing the Delhi batters to score freely kept Bengal in the match.Delhi suffered the greatest jolt when left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik got in-form Badoni (85) caught at first slip by Easwaran.Like the first innings, the Delhi tail did put up some resistance before folding up for 277 in the extended second session before the tea interval.Both Easwaran and Paul ensured smooth going. articles.title: 'Message we got after first 5 overs': How West Indies' clever 'plan' left Team India stumped in 4th T20I
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: West Indies pacer Keemo Paul said his team used slower deliveries well on a pitch that offered some grip to beat India by 24 runs in the fourth
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Indies pacer Keemo Paul said his team used slower deliveries well on a pitch that offered some grip to beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad on Wednesday. West Indies scored 247 for three before bowling India out for 223. Paul played a key role in defending the big total, taking five wickets to help the visitors secure the win.Slower deliveries and yorkers prove effectivePaul said the pitch was good for batting, but a few deliveries gripped the surface. The West Indies bowlers made the most of those conditions by using slower balls.“From the batters' perspective, the message we got after the first five overs was that it was a pretty good wicket. One or two balls were gripping, but other than that, it was pretty good,” Paul said in the post-match press conference.“As bowlers, the slower balls helped us here. On other wickets and at other grounds, we haven't been getting much grip, but it worked here,” he added.Paul struck at important moments during India's chase. He dismissed Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prince Yadav off successive deliveries before removing Axar Patel to seal the West Indies' victory.Explaining the bowling strategy, Paul said: “The game plan was to keep bowling into the wicket for as long as possible and execute our yorkers when we knew they were going for the big shots.”Team meetings help Paul execute his plansThe 28-year-old pacer said detailed discussions and a clear understanding of individual roles helped him deliver under pressure.“Every team has its own game plans. We sit together and discuss them, and we have some pretty long team meetings. I knew what I wanted to do, what my field settings would be and what my plan was. Obviously, I won't share my plan, but I think I executed it pretty well,” he said.No dew helped West Indies bowlersPaul also pointed to the absence of dew as an important factor in the match. He said the conditions helped the bowlers maintain a better grip on the ball while defending their total under lights.“Some pretty big scores have been chased in this series, but I think a key factor is that there was no dew (in Hyderabad). When there is dew, it becomes quite hard for teams bowling second. In the last game and this one, there was no dew, and I think we executed our plans perfectly,” he said.Hope's century gives West Indies a big totalPaul credited captain Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and the partnerships he built for giving the bowlers enough runs to defend.Shimron Hetmyer scored 33 off 12 deliveries, while Sherfane Rutherford remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls as West Indies posted 247 for three.Paul said the team's approach remained positive regardless of whether they batted first or chased a target.“Every game is the same for us. Whether we are batting first or batting second, we try to be as positive as possible. On these wickets, you have to score big. We did not win the toss today.“But I think Captain Hope has been fantastic for us. The key partnerships he built gave us the runs we needed. I think the team bowled really well,” Paul said.Paul also spoke about the challenges bowlers face in T20 cricket, especially on pitches that favour batters and offer very little room for mistakes.“You can't be too hard on yourself as a bowler on these tracks. The margin for error is very, very thin. It all comes down to execution. It is about taking it one day at a time and sticking to the process.“As long as you try to follow the team's plans as much as possible, I don't think the staff will have a problem. You can't be too tough on yourself on these wickets,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'The turning point was when Tilak Varma got out': Sanju Samson explains why India lost 4th T20I against West Indies
articles.summary: Sanju Samson has backed India's young fast bowlers despite their 24-run defeat to the West Indies in the fourth T20I, saying they need more matches and
articles.body: Sanju Samson has backed India's young fast bowlers despite their 24-run defeat to the West Indies in the fourth T20I, saying they need more matches and experience to improve. The India wicketkeeper-batter also pointed to Tilak Varma's dismissal as the key moment that changed the course of the chase.The defeat levelled the five-match series at 2-2, setting up a winner-takes-all decider in Bengaluru on Saturday. The West Indies posted 247 for three, powered by Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 off 50 balls, before Keemo Paul took five wickets to bowl India out for 223 in 19.3 overs.Tilak Varma's wicket proved decisive in India's chaseIndia began the chase aggressively, with Samson smashing 56 off just 23 balls, including six fours and four sixes. The hosts raced to 60 without losing a wicket in four overs, but Keemo Paul dismissed Samson and Ishan Kishan in the fifth over to shift the momentum.Samson felt Tilak's dismissal was the biggest turning point. Tilak scored 43 off 25 balls and was building a strong partnership with Reddy before his wicket weakened India's position."I think the turning point was when Tilak got out. As I said, we were cruising along nicely. Reddy and Tilak were putting the bowlers under pressure and batting really well," he said, as quoted by PTI.Samson also stood by Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma, insisting that one quiet outing should not lead to doubts about their ability."I think Ishan and Abhishek Sharma are two of the best batters in the world at the top of the order. You cannot really ask for more from them. One game (not scoring) is fine."Despite the loss, Samson said India were ready for the series decider and acknowledged the West Indies' strong performances."We are 2-2 now, and everything comes down to the game in Bengaluru. We are very charged up and want to go out there and compete against them. West Indies have been playing some really good cricket, and you have to give them credit for coming to India and dominating in two games," he added.Samson backs young bowlers, praises Shai HopeWith Jasprit Bumrah rested, India's bowling attack struggled to contain the visitors, as Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh conceded 52 runs each in their four overs. Samson said replacing Bumrah was not easy but expressed confidence in India's emerging pace options."He is a once-in-a-generation bowler, and we are very lucky to have him. But we also have some really good talent coming through. Arshdeep has been doing a great job, and the way Prince Yadav has bowled in the last few games has been very impressive."We have some really good quality talent, and the more we play them and back them, the more matches we give them, the better they will become," Samson said.He also credited Hope for his controlled batting, which helped the West Indies post a massive total."He has been playing really well, and we need to respect what he has been doing. He has been playing some really good cricketing shots without taking too many risks."We have to give him credit for the way he is batting, and we are definitely working on how to respond to him in every game," he said.Samson explained that Hyderabad's pitch, which offered good bounce, was suited to high-scoring matches. He added that teams must adjust their approach based on the conditions rather than follow the same plan everywhere."When you are playing on a high-scoring ground, you have to go into fifth gear from ball one. But if you are playing on a surface where the scores are around 160-170, like in the Lucknow game, where there was something in the wicket, your plans change accordingly."You cannot always play the same kind of cricket. You have to assess the conditions, the bounce and the situation," Samson said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's premier fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah is unlikely to feature in the five-ODI series against New Zealand because the Indian think-tank
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's premier fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah is unlikely to feature in the five-ODI series against New Zealand because the Indian think-tank wants him to focus on the red-ball leg of the tour. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Bumrah is completely fit, but the team management wants him to increase his workload by playing in the third India A fixture before joining the side for the series opener in Wellington.The India A fixture begins on November 6, and there is a sufficient gap between that game and the first Test in Wellington, which starts on November 19. It is further understood that Bumrah, who has already started his red-ball preparations in Ahmedabad, will reach the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) sometime later this month before flying to New Zealand."Bumrah is completely fit, but for a long tour, it's important to prioritise. The Test series is very important, so there's no point making Bumrah slog it out in the ODIs and then suddenly shift focus to red-ball cricket. He is the leader of the bowling pack, and a fresh, ready Bumrah is the priority right now," says a source tracking developments.It is worth noting that Bumrah last played a multi-day fixture against South Africa at home last year. A knee injury ruled him out of the two Tests against Sri Lanka earlier this year, but the Indian team management wants him ready and available for the upcoming Tests.Multiple discussions have taken place with key personnel, with the focus not just on New Zealand but also on the five Tests against Australia early next year. In the build-up to that series, a similar approach is expected, and keeping Bumrah away from inconsequential bilateral matches may not come as a surprise."The plan is not just for New Zealand, but discussions are also happening for the BGT next year. There is no point wasting Bumrah for inconsequential bilaterals. Right now, the WTC is the focus, and all energies will be directed at planning for that," adds the source.India's ODI and Test squads are likely to be announced in the next few days as the selectors continue to wait for updates on players like Harshit Rana, Prasidh Krishna and Rishabh Pant.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has urged Indian batters to take greater responsibility while chasing targets after their 24-run defeat to the West
articles.body: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has urged Indian batters to take greater responsibility while chasing targets after their 24-run defeat to the West Indies in the fourth T20 International in Hyderabad on Wednesday.India failed to chase West Indies’ huge total of 247 for three, despite Sanju Samson’s quickfire 56 off 23 balls. Keemo Paul picked up five wickets to bowl India out for 223, forcing the five-match series into a decider in Bengaluru.“The first thing this Indian side needs to improve is how they chase. The batting unit needs to show more responsibility. If the batters don’t take responsibility, this Indian side will not succeed,” Gavaskar told JioStar.He also felt India failed to make the most of the batting-friendly conditions, especially with dew helping the batters.Gavaskar questions India’s batting approachGavaskar said India should have built on the strong start provided by Samson, but the other batters failed to deliver.“Sanju gave India a great start, but the rest of the batters didn’t capitalise at all. Abhishek Sharma played a poor knock, which is not acceptable by his standards.“Ishan Kishan fell right into Keemo Paul’s trap, and Shreyas Iyer has not got going since his hundred,” he said.However, the former captain defended India’s inexperienced bowlers, saying they needed time to learn at the international level despite conceding a big score.“Yes, I know the bowling has been poor, but these bowlers are not experienced. They are new to international cricket, and they will need to get hit for boundaries, otherwise they will not learn,” he said.Pujara praises Shai Hope’s battingFormer India batter Cheteshwar Pujara praised West Indies captain Shai Hope, whose second century of the series helped his team post a massive total.“Hope has been a problem for India in this white-ball series and what stands out is that he does not rely on blind slogging. He backs his natural game and picks his gaps. That is why he scores so quickly without taking too many risks.“He's also a good player of spin because this pitch was a little challenging for the batters to dominate the spinners.“But he had a lot of clarity. When a batter has that kind of control, it becomes very difficult for the bowlers to build pressure,” said Pujara.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson believes Jasprit Bumrah is irreplaceable, but he is confident that the team has young bowlers who can improve with more opportunities. India lost the fourth T20I against the West Indies by 24 runs at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad on Wednesday. With Bumrah rested for the series, India's bowlers have faced a tough challenge on batting-friendly pitches.Bumrah was rested after participating in the Asian Games as the BCCI looks to manage the workload of its star fast bowler.Samson backs India's young bowlersSamson said Bumrah's quality makes him a special player, but he also pointed to the progress of Arshdeep Singh and Prince Yadav."There is no replacement for Jasprit Bumrah. He is a once-in-a-generation kind of bowler, and we are very lucky to have him. But we have had some really good talent coming along also; Arshdeep (Singh) has been doing a great job, and also the way Prince Yadav has bowled in the last few games is very impressive. I feel we have some really good talent. The more we play them, the more we back them, the better they will become," Samson said after the defeat.Arshdeep suffered a blow to his left arm while batting towards the end of India's innings. Samson said the team hoped the pacer would recover in time for the fifth T20I on Saturday."Arshdeep is putting ice on his shoulder," Samson said. "Hopefully he recovers soon."Samson praises West Indies captain HopeWest Indies captain Shai Hope has been in excellent form during the series. He has scored two centuries and a half-century in the four T20Is, after also hitting two centuries in the preceding ODI series.Samson said Hope deserved credit for the way he had handled the Indian bowling attack."He (Hope) is playing really well; we need to respect what he has been doing. He has been playing some really good cricketing shots, not taking that much risk, so he is respecting the bowlers as well."We need to give the credit to him for the way he is batting, and we are definitely switched on how to respond to him every game,” he added.Samson backs Abhishek and Ishan after Hyderabad defeatIndia's top order also came under focus after Abhishek Sharma scored 29 off 24 balls in the fourth T20I. articles.title: After Durban drubbing, South Africa drop Stubbs from squad; call up player with two Test experience and eye Rabada return
articles.summary: South Africa have called up Matthew Breetzke and left Tristan Stubbs out of their squad for the second Test against Australia in Gqeberha, coach Shukri
articles.body: South Africa have called up Matthew Breetzke and left Tristan Stubbs out of their squad for the second Test against Australia in Gqeberha, coach Shukri Conrad said on Thursday.The changes are likely to bring a reshuffle in South Africa's batting order for the Test, which starts on Sunday. Conrad also confirmed that Ryan Rickelton will take over as wicketkeeper. This could mean Kyle Verreynne is dropped, although he remains with the squad. Verreynne has not scored a Test half-century in his last 13 innings.The changes come after South Africa lost the first Test by 214 runs in Durban on Tuesday. Stubbs scored 33 runs across his two innings in the match at Kingsmead.Breetzke has played two Tests for South Africa, against Bangladesh in late 2024 and Zimbabwe last year. He has a first-class batting average of 37 and last played a first-class match in February. However, he scored a century in the first ODI against Australia last month."Matt has been part of the squad before and the fact that his ODI form is as hot as it is gave him an inside lane and also, more importantly, the attitude and the character Matt brings, and has, will go a long way," Conrad said.With Rickelton set to take the gloves, South Africa must also decide where he will bat. He could continue to open the innings while keeping wickets, as he has done before, or move down the order."With Ricks (Rickelton) taking the gloves, there are obviously decisions to be made over whether he does move down the order or whether he can continue to open the batting and take the gloves, which he has done before," Conrad said."We'll have a look at what the conditions are like, but there are a few things to consider before play starts."Breetzke could now open alongside Aiden Markram. Tony de Zorzi, meanwhile, remains unavailable as he continues to recover from the hamstring injury he suffered during last month's ODI series.South Africa are also expecting lead fast bowler Kagiso Rabada to return for the second Test. articles.title: 'Why attack the batter?': Sunil Gavaskar fumes as Shamar Joseph hits Arshdeep Singh
articles.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar criticised West Indies fast bowler Shamar Joseph after a delivery struck Arshdeep Singh on the shoulder during the
articles.body: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar criticised West Indies fast bowler Shamar Joseph after a delivery struck Arshdeep Singh on the shoulder during the fourth T20I in Hyderabad on Wednesday. Gavaskar also called on India's batters to take greater responsibility after the hosts lost the match by 24 runs. The defeat levelled the five-match series and set up a decider in Bengaluru on Saturday.West Indies scored 247 for three before bowling India out for 223. Keemo Paul took five wickets, while captain Shai Hope led the visitors with an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls.The incident took place towards the end of India's chase. A bouncer from Joseph hit Arshdeep on the shoulder, leaving the Indian pacer in pain.Despite the discomfort, Arshdeep continued batting with India needing 30 runs off the final ball. Captain Shreyas Iyer also urged him to retire hurt and leave the field, but Arshdeep chose to stay.On the next delivery, Arshdeep moved away from his stumps and tried to hit the ball for a boundary. Joseph bowled another short delivery towards his injured shoulder. This time, the ball missed Arshdeep and went away for four byes and a wide.Joseph's approach drew a sharp reaction from Gavaskar in the commentary box. The former India captain questioned why the West Indies pacer was bowling at the batter when his stumps were left unprotected."He is aiming at him," Gavaskar was heard saying on air. "Why attack the batter when the stumps are right there?"“If he is not ok, he should retire. He seems to be in pain. You do not want to aggravate that injury,” said Gavaskar.“Would it not be simpler to just aim at the stumps? He knows that he is moving away to the left. Just aim at the stumps. Don’t aim at him. He is aiming at him,” a furious Gavaskar saidArshdeep could not continue after the incident and was retired hurt on five. His injury could be a concern for India ahead of Saturday's series decider.Gavaskar also expressed concern over India's batting performance during the chase. Despite a quick start from Sanju Samson, the hosts failed to reach the target.The former captain said the batting unit needed to improve its approach when chasing big totals.“The first thing this Indian side needs to improve is how they chase. The batting unit needs to show more responsibility. If the batters don’t take responsibility, this Indian side will not succeed,” Gavaskar told JioStar.He felt India should have shown greater control with the bat, especially in conditions that were expected to help the chasing side.“On a pitch like this, with the dew coming in, you have to show the kind of dominance with the bat that a back-to-back T20 World Cup winning team should, but that was missing completely in this game,” he added.The fourth T20I win levelled the series, leaving both teams with everything to play for in the fifth and final match.The series decider will be played at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on Saturday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Zak Crawley signs new Kent contract after losing England deal
articles.summary: Zak Crawley signs a one-year contract extension with Kent after his England central contract was not renewed on Monday.
articles.body:
England batter Zak Crawley has signed a one-year contract extension with Kent to keep him at the county next summer.

The 28-year-old has agreed the new deal three days after his central contract was not renewed when the England and Wales Cricket Board released its updated list.

Crawley has not featured in a Test since the final game of last winter's Ashes tour in Sydney and last appeared for England in a one-day international in Sri Lanka in January.

He played in 12 County Championship matches for Kent this season as they won promotion back to Division One, making 608 runs with a top score of 89 among four half-centuries.

"It's an exciting time as we head back into Division One of the County Championship and I'm looking forward to the challenge of competing for Kent this coming summer," said Crawley.

"It's great to see so many young players coming through the system here, similar to my journey into first-team cricket, and I'm excited to help them settle into the first team and further their development for the long term."

The opener has made more than 180 appearances in all competitions for his home county since his debut in 2017.

Kent players 'deserve all credit' for promotion

Heads of cricket Cook and Arman leave Kent roles

Crawley has played in 64 Tests and nine ODIs for England but his position in the international set-up came under scrutiny during last winter's 4-1 series Ashes defeat.

"He is an extremely talented batter and is a huge presence in our dressing room," said director of cricket Simon Cook.

"His experience of playing around the world not only benefits us on the field, but he is always willing to pass on his knowledge to our younger batters, something that will benefit us in the long term."

articles.title: 'Would I be tempted?' Sikandar Raza breaks silence on retirement U-turn if Zimbabwe enters WTC
articles.summary: Zimbabwe's ODI and T20I captain Sikandar Raza has made it clear that his country's possible entry into the World Test Championship (WTC) for the 2027-30
articles.body: Zimbabwe's ODI and T20I captain Sikandar Raza has made it clear that his country's possible entry into the World Test Championship (WTC) for the 2027-30 cycle will not change his plan to retire after next year's 50-over World Cup in Africa.Zimbabwe will co-host the 2027 ODI World Cup with South Africa and Namibia. For the 40-year-old all-rounder, the tournament will offer an opportunity to play a World Cup on home soil towards the end of his career.“The fact that I am coming to the end of my career as well, and to have an opportunity to play a home World Cup is certainly a blessing for me from a personal point of view,” Raza said, as quoted by news agency PTI.“Every cricketer dreams of having retired or to retire after playing a cricketing World Cup,” he added.When asked whether Zimbabwe's potential entry into the WTC during the 2027-30 cycle could make him reconsider his retirement, Raza ruled out the possibility.“Would I be tempted? No, I will not be tempted. I have come to peace with the decisions that I am making in life.“I'll not be a guy who will, when the time comes, call it off and then say, 'I'm taking my retirement back.' It will not happen. That's not me,” he said.While Raza does not intend to extend his career, he believes playing in the WTC would help Zimbabwe improve as a cricketing nation. He said the team might take time to perform well in the competition initially, but the experience would help improve its results across formats.“If that happens, I will be the first guy who will be in support of that. If Zimbabwe is part of WTC, we might not be able to do well at the start, but one thing I do know…our cricketing growth eventually — not eventually, quickly — will go up. Our performances will get better, and not just in Test cricket,” he said.No home advantageRaza acknowledged that Zimbabwe, South Africa and Namibia could find it difficult to gain a home advantage at the 2027 World Cup, as the International Cricket Council (ICC) oversees the tournament's arrangements.“We'll try our best to gain some home advantage, but for ICC events, it's very difficult because the ICC is in control of everything.“But yeah, we will try and take some advantage where we can. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Low Test crowds prompt review
articles.summary: A senior South African cricket official pledges to order a review into the low crowd which attended the first Test against Australia in Durban.
articles.body:
A senior South African cricket official has pledged to order a review into the low crowd which attended the first Test against Australia in Durban.

Despite South Africa being the reigning world Test champions and Australia the number one-ranked side in the world, fewer than 20,000 fans attended across the five days.

Australia, who are touring South Africa for the first time since the 2018 sandpaper scandal, won by 214 runs and can wrap up the three-match series when the second Test gets under way in Gqeberha on Sunday.

"It is impossible to overlook our disappointment that just under 20,000 fans attended across the five days," said KwaZulu-Natal Cricket Union chief executive Heinrich Strydom.

"A Test match of this quality deserved greater support in the stands. This is something we will reflect on through a thorough internal review.

"We need to listen to our supporters, reconnect with our communities and continue to find ways to make Test cricket more accessible, engaging and appealing.

"Test cricket is part of our sporting heritage and its future depends on all of us."

Attendances for Test cricket have been declining in many places around the world, most notably in South Africa and the West Indies.

However, live sport does remain a big draw in South Africa.

While the Test against Australia was ongoing, a football cup final between Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns was being held across town in Durban which attracted more than 50,000 fans.

"While we recognise supporters face competing demands on their time and finances, we must also understand better what influences their decisions to attend and what more we can do to make live cricket an attractive and worthwhile experience," added Strydom.

Is Test cricket financially sustainable?

Rusty or something more? South Africa's concern after Australia loss

South Africa call up 'Aussie agitator' Breetzke

On the pitch, South Africa have responded to their heavy first-Test defeat by calling up "Aussie agitator" Matthew Breetzke.

Batter Breetzke has been added to the squad at the expense of Tristan Stubbs, who is left out for the second Test after making scores of 32 and one in Durban.

Wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne remains in the squad but loses the gloves, with Ryan Rickelton in line to keep wicket. Breetzke and the uncapped Marques Ackerman look set to come into the top order in place of Stubbs and Verreynne.

Earlier in the tour, Breetzke made a century in the first one-day international but drew the ire of the Australians when he pinched a single after a throw rebounded off his body.

Cricket Australia's own website said the 27-year-old "got under Australia's skin" and described him as an "Aussie agitator", while South Africa coach Shukri Conrad admitted Breetzke's temperament was a factor in his inclusion.

"The attitude and character that Matt brings and has, I think that will go a long way," said Conrad.

Breetzke has played two previous Tests, managing only 14 runs in three innings, and has not played a first-class match since February.

However, the right-hander has made a sublime start to his one-day international career, averaging almost 59 from 17 matches.

South Africa must avoid defeat in the second Test, starting on Sunday, to avoid losing the three-match series with a game to spare.

The 214-run loss in the first Test was the world champions' first defeat in captain Temba Bavuma's 13 matches in charge.

The hosts look likely to include attack leader Kagiso Rabada after the pace bowler missed the first Test as part of his recovery from a hamstring injury.

Australia will have their own decisions to make over the batting line-up after being forced into changes for the first Test.

Injuries to Cameron Green and Josh Inglis meant a first Test in 10 years for Nic Maddinson. The opener was called into the XI despite not playing a first-class game in the previous 19 months following treatment for testicular cancer.

With Maddinson at the top of the order, Matthew Renshaw shuffled down to number five and produced a career-best performance. The Middlesbrough-born left-hander made scores of 190 and 82, as well as claiming two wickets with his off-breaks.

Australia head coach Andrew McDonald said Green is "progressing well" from an abdominal injury, while Inglis has started batting again after suffering a broken finger.

If either or both are passed fit, it would possibly mean Maddinson sits out, with Renshaw once again pushed up to open.

articles.title: England women's A squad will play red-ball cricket in India to continue Ashes preparation
articles.summary: England A squads travel to India in November to play three T20s, three 50-over fixtures and a four-day game.
articles.body:
England A will play a four-day game on their upcoming tour of India as part of their preparation for next summer's Women's Ashes.

The tour takes place in November and December, and also includes three T20s and three 50-over matches as England face another winter without any senior international cricket.

While the home international summer ended with a 3-0 thrashing of Ireland in September, England do not have any other fixtures scheduled until after Christmas.

Though the dates have not been confirmed, England are scheduled to play three T20s and three one-day internationals against Sri Lanka before the first Women's Champions Trophy - a T20 competition - takes place in India in February.

That is followed by a series against West Indies in April, which could include a Test match , although those dates have also not yet been finalised.

Some players have been signed for Australia's Women's Big Bash League while the Women's Premier League in India will also take place before the home season of 2027 begins.

Eleven players included in the England A squad across all three formats have been capped internationally, including established fast bowlers Issy Wong and Lauren Filer and emerging left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman.

They are included alongside all-rounders Mady Villiers, Charis Pavely and Jodi Grewcock, wicketkeeper-batter Kira Chathli and seamer Grace Ballinger.

Seamer Ryana Macdonald-Gay is included in both white-ball squads while top-order batter Grace Scrivens is part of the 50-over and four-day sides.

Batter Davina Perrin has been added to England's performance programme, but is recovering from injury and therefore will not be going on the A tour, as well as fast bowler Cassidy McCarthy.

The tour starts with the T20s in Pune on 30 November, followed by the 50-over fixtures and the four-day game at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium.

The multi-format Ashes series, which has been played as such since 2013, starts with a four-day Test on 27 June at Headingley.

An improved England, who reached the final of the Women's T20 World Cup earlier this year under Charlotte Edwards and Nat Sciver-Brunt, will be aiming to regain the Ashes after a dismal 16-0 thrashing away from home in 2025.

articles.title: Lord's pitch dug up after 'unsatisfactory' rating by ICC and demerit point following England vs New Zealand Test
articles.summary: Pitch 9, which is one of five central strips at Lord's, was handed its first demerit point and deemed as "unsatisfactory" by the ICC after first England vs New Zealand Test in June; the MCC has recently re-laid the pitch following a review of the Lord's square
articles.body:
Pitch 9, one of five central strips at Lord's, was handed its first demerit point and deemed "unsatisfactory" by the ICC after match referee Andy Pycroft found excessive seam movement and inconsistent bounce during this summer's Test against the Kiwis.

All 40 wickets fell in just 166 overs during the match.

In response, the MCC has recently re-laid the pitch following a review of the Lord's square.

Work to reconstruct the pitch began earlier this month.

The MCC told members this week that the decision to dig up the pitch was taken after the most comprehensive review of Lord's pitch conditions.

The MCC also plans to use hybrid pitches, which the data has found to be more durable than traditional pitches. Hybrid pitches are not permitted to be used in Tests.

The club is also producing the first of three drop-in trays, which will be moved to the main square in 2028.

The 'permanent drop-ins' will be installed on a long-term basis, rather than being removed and replaced seasonally like those found at multi-use venues in Australia.

Lord's is currently scheduled to stage two Tests next year - against Bangladesh in May and Australia at the end of June in the Ashes.

The Kia Oval has been chosen as the host venue for the World Test Championship final.

articles.summary: India women's cricket vice-captain Shafali Verma said the team is focused on playing fearless but smart cricket as it begins its preparations for the
articles.body: India women's cricket vice-captain Shafali Verma said the team is focused on playing fearless but smart cricket as it begins its preparations for the Women's Champions Trophy at home early next year.India will face Zimbabwe for the first time in a bilateral series, starting with three T20Is in Raipur before the teams move to Vadodara for three ODIs. We are just trying to keep growing series by series,” Shafali told reporters on the eve of the opening match.India have also seen a change in leadership after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down. She said the time away helped her identify areas that needed improvement, including consistency, fitness and mental strength.“I analysed myself when I was out of the team. I needed to work on consistency, fitness, and mental growth.
